LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:942-945, [[combat-core/the-in-combat-stance-gate-is-reload-48-of-a-192-max]], ends: 'So the in-combat stance switch costs no Focus and no Chi: it needs the reload meter at 48/192 = 25%.' I read §1t3489s0§ in full, :3083 to :3177: the setter's tail is :3160 'if(§1t1525s0§.§1t9948s0§())' -> :3162 'this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48;' -> :3163-3166 clamp at 0 -> :3169 repaint the bar. It costs 48. text: THE FREE/CHARGED SPLIT IS REAL BUT THE GATE IS NOT SPLIT, AND EVERY WRITE-UP OF THIS CLUSTER SO FAR HAS BLURRED IT. The 48-Focus DEBIT is inside the battle predicate (§1t99s0§.as:3160-3162). The ENTRY GATE is not: §1t4470s0§ at :3048-3051 is 'return this.§1t4469s0§() && this.§1t4414s0§ >= 48;' and §1t4472s0§ opens at :3060 with 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48) { return; }' — neither is wrapped in §1t9948s0§()/isBattle(). And the caller that reaches them outside a fight is the GLOBAL input handler, §1t1541s0§.as:605-615: 'case Keyboard.SPACE: _loc2_ = §1t1523s0§.§1t9586s0§(); if(!§1t10074s0§ && _loc2_.§1t4470s0§()) { _loc2_.§1t4472s0§(); ...Snd_smallClick } else { ...Snd_error }' — not a battle-only widget, unlike the BattleUI button at §1t113s0§.as:468-480. So the correct rule is THREE-part, not two: out of combat the switch costs nothing but still requires reload >= 48; in combat it requires reload >= 48 and spends 48. A recreation that ships 'free and unrestricted' overworld switching is wrong, and the error is invisible in play only because reload refills +1/tick (§1t99s0§.as:1203-1205) and the overworld HUD hides the bar entirely — which I confirmed on film at reference/frames/combat_frames/Nr4fQstqHDM_t0425s.png, crop (150,930)-(620,1080) 3x LANCZOS: two bars and the words 'HEAVY STANCE', no third bar.

ledger_text: LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:3644 — 'The third bar carries the status text CANNOT CHANGE STANCE when it is below a sixth of max.'
text: A BUILD LEAK INSIDE A SURVIVING FINDING, EXACTLY THE C2 TRAP. LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:3644, [[ui-hud/in-combat-hud-is-three-bars]], says 'The third bar carries the status text CANNOT CHANGE STANCE when it is below a sixth of max.' A SIXTH is the ANDROID rule: MCSPlayer.as:2977 'if(this.reload < this.maxreload / 6) return;' over maxreload = 5 * 24 = 120 (:239), i.e. 20. The WEB build has no sixth anywhere in this path: §1t113s0§.as:328 draws the bar as '(param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48)' and shows the grey caption only at ratio == 0 (:336-343), over maxreload = 8 * 24 = 192 (§1t99s0§.as:249) — so the caption is on while reload <= 48, a QUARTER of max, and the threshold is the same flat 48 the stance gate uses (:3050, :3060). The finding names no build, which under §3(c) makes it the defective side rather than a genuine contradiction. Consequence if shipped as written: on a 192-tick meter the caption would clear at 32 instead of 48, and a stance switch would be offered for 16 ticks while the code still refuses it — the one visible state the whole cluster exists to reproduce.

lane_impact: L5 combat-core: the Focus-full state is (i) x1.3 on your own damage roll, unconditional, and (ii) hit-negation ONLY during SLASH_STATE with the stance passive owned.
text: The full-Focus evade is not a passive damage immunity on a full bar: its first term is §1t4465s0§(), defined at §1t99s0§.as:2963-2966 as 'return actionState == §1t11149s0§;'. Structural twin fixes the name - in both files that function is the fourth 'return actionState == X' member and is immediately followed by 'internal function movement(...)': android MCSPlayer.as:2885-2888 is 'internal function isSlashing() : Boolean { return actionState == SLASH_STATE; }' followed by 'internal function movement(speed:int)'. So the rule is: while you are in SLASH_STATE, with reload == maxreload, and you own that stance's passive, an incoming hit is consumed for zero damage. A port that models it as 'full bar = untouchable' will be wrong in every non-slashing frame. The predicate appears four times, not twice: §1t99s0§.as:3383 and :3707 plus §1t4909s0§.as:74 and :311, and only the :3383 copy plays Snd_jump.

text: The same buff renders in two different places depending on scene, which no banked finding states. In the OVERWORLD frame t0425 the HUD stack under the portrait is exactly three rows - green HP 20/20, blue Chi 26/26, and the words 'HEAVY STANCE' - with no third bar and no banner; the active buff instead sits bottom-right of the screen as '150% DAMAGE' in yellow followed by '28:28' in white, a mm:ss countdown. In the BATTLE frame t0435, ten seconds later in the same longplay, the identical buff is a yellow '150% DAMAGE' banner directly under the three-bar stack with NO timer, and the third (Focus) bar has replaced the stance-name row. So: overworld = 2 bars + stance name + timed bottom-right buff list; battle = 3 bars + untimed buff banner below the stack. A ui-hud port that renders buffs in one place is wrong in one of the two scenes, and the buff TIMER exists only in the overworld readout.

text: Anyone porting the battle HUD from the android blobs will draw the third bar wrong. Web v0.717 normalises it at 48: §1t113s0§.as:328 'var _loc3_:Number = (param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48);'. Android v0.682 normalises the SAME bar at 24: MCSPlayer.as:3272 'StageManager.getBattleUI().updateReload((this.reload - 24) / (this.maxreload - 24));' and :1163-1168 'this.tempreload = this.reload - 24; ... updateReload(this.tempreload / (this.maxreload - 24));'. The AI's own low-Focus branch uses the same android constant — MCSPlayer.as:4528 'else if(this.reload < 24 && dice == 0)' against the web build's §1t4904s0§.as:632 'else if(§1t4414s0§ < 24 && _loc1_ == 0)', so 24 survives in one place on web too. Both builds compute the same capacity (48 + SPD*6: §1t1523s0§.as:2276 and android StatsManager.as:1841), so the divergence is purely in where the bar's zero point sits — and on web that zero point is the same 48 that gates the stance cycler.
